security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown links and code formatting. One instruction runs local ESP connector and ledger commands; it is legitimate functionality but should execute only with user confirmation and validated values.

remediation.issue: Optional connector commands process ESP data and include a placeholder list argument.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before running connector commands. Pass the list name as a validated argument, not through shell interpolation, and document the data scope.

content.value_statement: Email lists can lose engagement and develop deliverability problems between campaigns. This skill turns your ESP data into clear cohorts, trend checks, and an action worklist.
actual_capabilities: Groups subscribers by 30, 90, 180, and 365-day engagement recency.
Compares hard-bounce and spam-complaint rates with a prior baseline.
Checks suppression-list growth and identifies potential opt-out leakage.
Creates sized re-permission, sunset, and prune worklist segments.
Labels conclusions as measured, estimated, or needing more input.
Produces SEND list-hygiene and engagement-decay handoff reads.
limitations: It relies on ESP exports, prior baselines, or an optional compatible connector.
It does not verify authentication settings or calculate a complete email quality score.
It does not own consent records or make final compliance decisions.
It cannot infer trend changes when no prior baseline is available.

use_cases.title: Review a growing newsletter list
use_cases.description: Identify dormant subscribers and prepare a measured sunset plan before deliverability declines.

use_cases.title: Investigate declining campaign engagement
use_cases.description: Compare current bounce and complaint signals with an earlier export and prioritize follow-up actions.

use_cases.title: Maintain a recurring hygiene process
use_cases.description: Create a monthly or quarterly worklist with documented baselines for a marketing operations team.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic list review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my email list health. I will provide an ESP engagement export and bounce report. Create cohorts and a simple action worklist.

prompt_templates.title: Compare with a baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this month's engagement, hard-bounce, and complaint data with last quarter's baseline. Show the numeric changes and recommended actions.

prompt_templates.title: Check suppression drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these active-list and suppression exports for growth, leakage, and subscribers who need re-permission, sunset, or pruning.

prompt_templates.title: Run a scheduled hygiene watch
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a quarterly hygiene review for our newsletter profile. Use these exports and baseline, label evidence quality, produce SEND S and E reads, and state the next comparison date.

output_examples.input: Analyze a list with 21,000 subscribers and 3,100 never-engaged subscribers.
output: Cohort finding: 3,100 subscribers are never engaged, or 15 percent of the active list.
Action: sunset this cohort from regular sends and review clean addresses for one re-permission attempt.
Evidence: measured cohort count; trend needs a prior baseline.

output_examples.input: Compare a 0.12 percent complaint rate with a prior 0.06 percent rate.
output: Trend: complaint rate increased by 0.06 percentage points and exceeds the 0.1 percent watch line.
Action: pause expansion of active sending and route the hygiene read to the email-quality auditor.
Next step: investigate recent sources, suppression handling, and affected cohorts.

best_practices: Provide a dated ESP export and a prior baseline for every scheduled review.
Keep opt-out and suppression records authoritative in the consent system.
Confirm worklist changes before removing or suppressing subscribers.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a point-in-time rate as a trend without a baseline.
Do not re-mail complained or hard-bounced addresses through a re-permission campaign.
Do not mark incomplete data as a passing hygiene result.

faq.question: What data do I need?
faq.answer: Provide engagement data, bounce and complaint data, and preferably a dated prior baseline.

faq.question: Can it work with cohort totals?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use cohort totals, but it labels derived rates as estimated.

faq.question: Does it delete subscribers?
faq.answer: No. It produces a worklist and asks for confirmation before saved results or downstream actions.

faq.question: Does it check SPF or DKIM?
faq.answer: No. Use the separate deliverability pre-flight skill for authentication checks.

faq.question: What is suppression leakage?
faq.answer: It is an opt-out or suppressed address that remains eligible for active sending.

faq.question: Can I use it every month?
faq.answer: Yes. Each completed review can become the baseline for the next scheduled comparison.
